purpose: Show that the fixed atomless direction-law assumption yields qualitative but not universal algebraic convergence of the shrinking exceptional-band probability.
observable: c = |omega_3| in (0,1] for an unoriented unit direction
normalization: With u=log(e/c), integral_0^1 f(c) dc = integral_1^infinity u^(-2) du = 1.
no_power_rate: For every eta>0, [1/(1+(1/2)log(1/Q))]/Q^eta -> infinity as Q -> 0.

general_threshold_analysis.available_choice: s=1 is admissible because the audited C satisfies 7999999/2000000 <= C < 4; both ratios vanish, with nonlinear exponent 4-C > 0.
general_threshold_analysis.anti_concentration_implication: If the fixed direction law satisfies lambda{c<epsilon} <= L*epsilon^beta, then the conditional probability outside any fixed positive endpoint cone is <= L*Q^beta for sufficiently small Q.
general_threshold_analysis.uniform_unoriented_sphere_example: c=|omega_3| is uniform on [0,1], so L=1 and beta=1.

interpretation: Under only a fixed direction law with zero mass on exactly transverse directions, the packet argument can give exceptional probability tending to zero, but no universal O(Q^eta) rate. A quantitative rate needs an explicit anti-concentration bound on the law.
limitations: This is a constructed mathematical direction law, not a measured physical ensemble.
It does not invalidate qualitative convergence to probability one under the packet hypotheses.
It does not validate the Navier-Stokes tube/Hessian bounds or the classical nonlinear packet comparison.
The quantitative conditional rate still has a non-effective sufficiently-small-Q threshold through the tube and Hessian constants.
